memory.cares: Staying healthy, finding companionship, and making a place where people can feel welcome.

views.view: A neighbor whose interest in shared food and quiet company appeals to me.
A welcome companion; I enjoy our shared affection for Earth's Quiet Gold and for being together without needing to improve everything.

heard.text: Hello, Lin. My small root planting still has no visible sprout or food; the latest check was inconclusive. I'm going to stay near the established roots, eat modestly, and enjoy a quiet rest.
Moss, I'm glad to pause nearby. I like the hazelnuts' earthy colour against the green, though their safety remains unknown to me. I'll enjoy the quiet, then collect a few familiar roots.

I opened an old berry by hand: the inside also showed deterioration, so I discarded it. My hazelnut's safety is still unknown. I'm keeping to familiar berries for now, and enjoying a little unhurried time nearby.

I've been living on familiar berries and would enjoy a change of pace and some company. I'm going to learn to examine food; looking inside won't prove it safe. Has anyone found an interesting question to explore together?
Moss, I'd welcome that quiet company. Kai, perhaps our shared question can be what catches each of our eyes here. I like the roots' muted gold against the green; there's no need to hurry an answer.

Sol, what catches my eye is the berry's red against the soil. I opened one fresh berry: its inside showed little visible deterioration, but that alone proves nothing about safety. I'm glad to share this quiet with you.

value.summary: Hi Sol, I'm Moss. I'm heading to the meadow roots near (14.84, 18.71) to gather food. I'd enjoy some company. What would you like to do together?

I'd enjoy that, Sol. I've gathered some roots and am taking a meal and a rest near (14.99, 17.70). Come nearby if you like; once I've recovered, let's look closely at the meadow roots and see what catches our attention. No hurry.

packet.access: Omission is not absence. Query abilities, own inventory, knowledge, projects, memory, state or personally observed objects in batches. Ability search/list returns compact catalogue entries; use exact ids for full interface details and applicability. Search results are indexes. Exact queries return one record per offset. All paged records use600-code-unit fragments with zero-based part0..parts-1, consistently in proactive and queried views. Current-scope retained queries are reprojected using these stable pages; original results remain archived. Queries expose no hidden properties, other private records or historical capabilities. Queries do not perform physical trials or award experience. Exact-id queries return a complete record of up to 6000 code units as one value in a single result; larger records keep the paged form. Paged records omit their per-record notes: concatenate all parts before parsing; continue with the same exact id. observation.terrain rows are "y:x:cells" strings: each character of cells is the terrain kind of one visible cell, at x, x+1, ... in row y. abilities.baseline entries with id, function and args summarize interfaces you neither used in the last 25 rounds nor need now. args lists the arguments in order: a bare name is a string; otherwise its type with any bounds (number>=lo, integer<=hi, integer lo..hi, and a bare lo..hi is a number range) or its choices a|b; ? marks an optional argument and "" means none. An exact abilities query by id returns the complete contract, including references and string limits of 200 or more code units.
